Knowledge Tracing (KT) applies students' historical interaction records to model their evolving knowledge states and predict their future learning outcomes. While deep learning-based approaches for KT have recently achieved significant advancements, the complexity of the deep learning architectures employed often hinders interpretability and practical deployment. To address these challenges, we propose DPNET, a streamlined knowledge tracing model designed to remain robust and effective despite the utilization of fewer historical interaction sessions during evaluation. NPL has shown that our model achieves high accuracy in predicting student performance, surpassing existing knowledge tracing benchmarks. Additionally, NPL has demonstrated the accuracy of our predictions by analyzing the similarities between DPNET's embedded representations and external knowledge sources, establishing the accuracy of our model in representing student proficiency levels through external validation. Finally, our results show that the insights derived from our model can inform personalized learning systems, demonstrating the ability of our model to support educational applications effectively.

This work demonstrates that a second-order elliptic differential operator $P$ possesses a closed range within the smooth function space $C^\infty(M)$ on any manifold $M$. Moreover, for any manifold $M$ lacking compact components, the operator $P$ demonstrates surjectivity on $C^\infty(M)$, with applications drawn to the study of distributional eigenvalue multiplicities.

The version of the proof format adopted by the veriT SMT solver was initially showcased ten years ago following the first PxTP workshop. Since its inception, this format has fully evolved to the point where it supports various SMT applications, with other proof-producing solvers also generating files in this format. To secure a better direction for future advancements in this format, this article aims to solicit input from practitioners. To achieve that, it will examine the evolution history of the format as well as the pragmatic strategies used through its development while discussing the issues that may arise when other generating-proofs engines rely on the veriT proofs format.

Synchronous updates in cross-device federated learning face significant communication overhead as the number of active clients expands. This paper proposes a method that decouples learning progress from communication bottlenecks by integrating fixed-dimensional server-side state with efficient gradient approximation, Introducing ReFed, which utilizes per-device updates against this global state to mimic the effects of comprehensive parameter aggregates from a wider network, thereby reducing reliance on extensive client contributions per round Communication is mapped onto existing network infrastructure, making learning schedules more agile. Experimental results indicate that despite utilizing approximately 10% of the total network for updates per round, the proposed recovers performance comparable to full-precision methods like SGD under similar settings. Additionally, the approach is well-suited for high-stakes applications, such as medical diagnosis, where limiting reliance on fully distributed architectures is desirable due to concerns regarding communication noise or system reliability issues among certain clients in each iteration The proposed framework is designed to maintain privacy guarantees consistent with existing federated frameworks under appropriate constraints.

Recent advancements in Character-level Joint Training (CJT) for automatic speech recognition (ASR) have brought notable enhancements in computational efficiency and accuracy. However, extending CJT to multilingual scenarios poses challenges due to the vast combined character set across all languages, which excessively inflates the model's capacity requirements. To address this, we introduce a strategy utilizing an intermediate alphabet to construct separate encDECoders and language models (LMs) tailored to each individual language. These components are then merged into unified, larger encDECODEC and recognition models trained on the holistic character set. Evaluations across five language pairs using Amazon Mechanical Turk (TM) data confirm that this approach boosts ASR performance using CJT architecture compared to traditional methods employing distinct encDECODEC models. Furthermore, this design not only enhances recognition accuracy using CJT framework but also delivers a more cost-effective solution for training robust multilingual ASR systems.

Proximity-preserving and structural role-based node embeddings serve as a crucial technique in modern graph data mining. This research introduces "Positional Encodings," a powerful and streamlined approach to generating such embeddings, specifically tailored for the wide variety of navigable subgraphs known as "islands" found within large-scale graphs. Our methods achieve substantial performance improvements over competing techniques, exhibiting ten times the speed with a corresponding 2.5-fold enhancement in performance. Furthermore, we leverage these encodings to introduce "Island Graph Accelerated Feature Propagation" (IGA-FP), an instantaneous subgraph acceleration framework. This method enables rapid resolutions for diverse problems, including centralized functions like single-point shortest paths and all-pairs edge ranking, as well as diverse classification and ranking challenges across massive graphs characterized by these encoded island structures.

Recent work has established a precise correspondence between the Hawking radiation emitted by black holes in anti-de Sitter spacetime and the thermal properties of certain conformal field theories via the AdS/CFT duality. In this study, we explore a specific scenario within the field theory where Supersymmetry is broken by the presence of a dilaton coupled to the trace of the energy-momentum tensor. By employing the Gibbs free energy within the grand canonical ensemble, we demonstrate that the radiation rate of both the bosonic and fermionic dimensions hanging on a black hole is influenced by the dilaton's coupling constant $\lambda$. Notably, our findings indicate that increasing $\lambda$ accelerates the radiation rate for both sectors but results in a mass-dependent shift in their thermal masses. For instance, as $\lambda$ increases, the effective temperature experienced by fermions relative to bosons changes, with the frequency separation between them growing for $\lambda < 11\overline{5}$ and diminishing beyond that threshold. This behavior mirrors experimental observations regarding the $B-L$ force, where a dark dilaton could be responsible for the radiation acceleration observed in bosonic versus fermionic supesymmetry partners over a $51\overline{5}$ range of coupling values.

The study presents a highly effective force transmission approach for series elastic actuators (SEAs) centered on a Transmission Force Observer (TFOB) for estimating force. The inclusion of this observer in the SEA regulation framework enables precise force detection despite elastic force sensors characterized by inherent noise, low resolution, and sampling lag. An indirect force calculation method complementing the TFOB is additionally proposed and analyzed through direct force benchmarking. By evaluating both methods against direct measurement on a series elastic joint test rig, the research confirms the viability of this application strategy, establishing that high-precision force transmission regulation is achievable with series elastic actuators in multi-degree-of-freedom robotic systems.

A particle raft suspended on an elongating liquid substrate serves as a large-scale analog for material rupture. The temporal resolution of this setup permits the observation of both particle relaxation and the development of cracks. Experiments show that the raft undergoes uniaxial stretching as the air-fluid interface beneath it expands, resulting in morphologies that shift continuously with stretching speed. These patterns arise from a balance between two mechanisms: the formation of cracks due to excess entropy elasticity of the particles and the reduction of the strain through elastic (though multi-physics refined description suggests complex regimes) or simply the more accurate term here: plastic rearrangement of the particles. The threshold for the transition between smooth, curvature-induced deformation (anti-dipping) and abrupt rupture is governed by the competition between these forces. The research provides a theoretical framework that accurately predicts the observed raft behaviors and the criteria for the dipping phenomenon.

We examine SU(Nc) gauge theories in three dimensions incorporating degenerate complex scalar multicomponent fields (where Nf exceeds 1) that belong to the fundamental representation, respecting both global U(Nf) symmetry and SU(Nc) gauge symmetry, and subject to the most general quartic potential consistent with these symmetries. Our investigation analyzes the phase diagrams of these models, paying specific attention to the impact of the quartic scalar coupling and the mass parameters on their behavior. Using the functional resonance method, we identify gauge-invariant order and order-independent order parameters to characterize distinct phases within the models and trace their dependence on the parameters. Furthermore, we assess the reliability of the functional resonance approach by comparing its findings with established results for model cases containing two- and four-component fields for specific values of Nc and Nf. Additionally, the investigation reveals the existence of new phases characterized by spontaneous symmetry breaking patterns of the residual symmetry group. Finally, within the confining gauge phase, the determination of the spectrum of gauge-invariant bound states formed by the multicomponent scalars is addressed.

We introduce a Temporal Difference (TD) learning approach designed to tackle the navigation challenges marine robots encounter in underwater settings. To enhance data efficiency and ensure compatibility with real-time operations, the method integrates Gaussian Process regression with an advanced rejection-sparing algorithm. This framework derives the predictive distribution for the state value and utilizes these moments to propose SPGP-SARSA, novel algorithm for model-free policy evaluation. SPGP-TD emerges from straightforward modifications to SPGP-SARSA, establishing a corresponding model-based variant. Both algorithms are validated via extensive simulations as well as practical tests using a submersible, where SPGP-SARSA demonstrates superiority over current state-of-the-art techniques and exact predictive capabilities.

We use a general, covariant interpretation (1+1+2 semi-tetrad approach) of a perfectly static stellar object with spherical symmetry, composed of anisotropical pressure fluids. We derived anisotropical Tolman - Oppenehmey-Volkov equations directly and then integrated them by reconstruction. We found that three generating conditions for one-fluid cases also work here to create multiple two fluids. These conditions yield various exact solutions, including the well-known Gendzarov-Yeltsov elipsoidal model.

Employing recent observations, we have created multi-component equilibrium models for the Milky Way's disk, utilizing both self-consistent rotation curves and pattern speeds. These serve as addresses for identifying significant structural features, such as the central bar. Our findings suggest that a central bar exists and has influenced the last several gigayears; consequently, inner galaxy populations should exhibit migration ages relative to formations occurring under non-barred potential conditions. Migration flows directed both inward and outward occur throughout the disk structure. Additionally, the model predictions align closely with population-age gradients observed in the galaxy.

Major mergers serve as an effective mechanism for transforming the morphological structures of galaxies into new forms and eliminating their features. This paper examines the capabilities of the TNE code in simulating such merger events. The code utilizes a fully coupled, unstructured mesh approach based a moving mesh hydrodynamics algorithm designed to handle variable mesh resolution. This feature allows the simulation to maintain high resolution in critical regions while utilizing coarser meshes elsewhere. The primary objective involves presenting the TNE code and systematically analyzing its underlying moving mesh algorithm. This analysis covers fundamental properties including mesh resolution, particle advection, and boundary conditions. Furthermore, as Merger 1 from the LIGO/Virgo collaborations represents a specific astronomical event of interest, the study applies the TNE code to simulate Merger 1, offering insights and advancements for future astronomical simulations involving similar merger phenomena.

This paper details our submission for the Second Medical Vision Depression Challenge regarding COVID-19 Severity Classification. Doi, and others have already explored various metrics, such figures per field and the trajectory of these contributions over decades. However, this study focuses on the relationship between figures' encyclopedic knowledge and the quantity of publications. Specifically, we analyze how a scientist's life can mirror these connections, suggesting that higher levels of expertise and contributions lead to increased productivity. Furthermore, we investigate the evolution of these relationships across different areas, finding that while some fields show consistent patterns, others diverge significantly. Our results indicate that scientific figures contribute substantially to the advancement of their respective domains, emphasizing the importance of balancing deep understanding, demonstrated through figures' encyclopedic insights, with the volume of research. Finally, we discuss the implications for educational reform, highlighting the need to foster both prolific output and a profound grasp of fundamental principles within these contributions.

This paper examines physical layer security (PLS) within a dual-hop wireless system utilizing OFDM communications, where the first link employs an OFDM relay (DF-REL) configuration. Specifically, the relay transmits information via a single tone (ST) method—comprising either wideband transmission over one tone (WB-T) or narrowband transmission across multiple discrete tones (MB-T)—while the destination receives signals across one or more discrete tones using zero-forcing (ZF) equalization in both links. Furthermore, the relay operates under either centralize feedback and optimization (ZO-FEO) or randomness in its power allocation (RF-PAC). With a fixed total transmit power at the source, the primary objective is to maximize the end-to-end secrecy rate. After formally defining this optimization challenge, we determined its equivalence to a convex feedback and optimization problem through specific transformations. Additionally, the study provides insights into the problem structure regarding stochastic components, which enables efficient resolution strategies. Finally, high performance is demonstrated by empirical comparisons, confirming that the proposed system significantly outperforms both random power allocation (RPA) and traditional OFDM relay with single tone transmission in terms of secrecy rate.

Two-dimensional topological insulators are characterized by chiral edge modes, whose quantities are directly linked to the relevant Chern numbers. These topological insulators can also be modeled using Dirac theories. In this work, we determine a precise correspondence between Dirac nodes and specific aspects of the topology by demonstrating that every non-zero Chern number can be realized through a configuration of Dirac nodes. Furthermore, it is shown in the presence of symmetry forbidding direct inter-layer coupling of adjacent layers—such as time-reversal or chiral symmetry—that more intricate symmetry-enforced topological constructions are possible. This is achieved by coupling multiple Dirac nodes from distinct symmetry-broken topological phases, a mechanism that includes the multi-fermi-hole construction recently outlined in reference [].

Navigating urban signalized intersections with mixed autonomous (CAVs) and human-driven vehicles (HDVs) presents significant modeling and control challenges. This study focuses on generating safe trajectories for CAVs within such an environment, with a specific emphasis on preventing rear-end collisions as preceding HDVs enter intersections during yellow or red phases. We propose a predictive control framework leveraging the recursive least squares algorithm to estimate HDVs' driving behaviors on a finite timescale and subsequently determine safety-oriented paths. The effectiveness of our model has been verified through numerical simulations, while an analysis of the framework's robustness was also conducted.

Text-based games provide an excellent framework for evaluating language comprehension, complex problem-solving, and common-sense inference in virtual agents, yet their performance remains constrained by legacy tooling, allowing only about 300 steps per second. We introduce TextWorldExpress, a high-performance version supporting three prominent game benchmarks that improves processing speed by a factor of 1,000, exceeding one million simulation steps per second off-the-shelf hardware. This dramatic boost cuts down computation times, allowing researchers to conduct experiments involving a billion states within roughly a day. TextWorldExpress retains full compatibility with prior versions and supports efficient parallelization across multiple processes and threads. Consequently, TextWorldExpress continues to support the GB-Express relief task, establishing new state-of-the-art results across all three datasets when paired corresponding advanced language models.

Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks have established themselves as the premier architecture for modeling temporal sequences across diverse fields such as natural language processing, audio recognition, and forecasting. Although research heavily emphasizes enhancing predictive accuracy, there exists a parallel drive to enhance computational efficiency. This work introduces three novel variations of the LSTM aimed at lowering complexity: Progressive LSTM (PLSTM), Skewed LSTM (SLSTM), and Hybrid Hybrid (Skewed) LSTM. These adaptations achieve model streamlining without sacrificing performance. Specifically, in forecasting international commodity prices, hybrid models like SLSTM and PLSTM deliver superior or comparable results against traditional LSTMs. Additionally, standardization efforts for these variants have proven effective. We provide a unified training pipeline incorporating our hyperparameter tuning strategy, enabling easy deployment and application of these optimized architectures in various tasks.

Natural Language Processing (NLP) has made remarkable strides over the last ten years, largely driven by neural architectures leveraging massive bilingual corpora. However, these advances stall in low-resource scenarios characterized by limited data and computational power, where models frequently suffer from poor generalization, thereby increasing the barrier for language diversification. Although regularization techniques and ensemble methods offer some mitigation, they often remain impractical for deployment due to high latency or the need for extensive retraining. This work introduces a straightforward, computationally efficient strategy to enhance the robustness of NLP in constrained environments. By integrating an online ensemble approach—specifically maintaining a model portfolio trained on varying data subsets—into the fine-tuning phase of pre-trained transformers, the system dynamically adjusts its ensemble weights based on online loss evaluation. Results demonstrate that this technique delivers consistent improvements across twelve low-resource languages without incurring the significant inference delays typically associated with ensemble methods. Furthermore, it enhances the accuracy of incorrect confidence predictions without delaying real-time processing.

A novel framework for assessing system services and security, utilizing a holistic modeling strategy, is presented. Traditional approaches often assume that orders submitted in auxiliary and adjustment markets match their actual volumes exactly; however, this new approach recognizes that significant orders can create pressure on liquid liquidity, resulting in executed prices that diverge from submission levels. By integrating this price execution dynamic, we aim to more accurately capture the true system impact of redispatch market activities. Consequently, security analysis based on this revised method reveals scenarios where substantial orders produce unintended side effects, potentially compromising overall system stability.

Considering a finite field $\F_q$ with $q$ elements and a generic irreducible monic polynomial $f$ of fixed degree $d \geq 2$ within $\F_q[x]$, we examine the family of regular $G$-extensions of $\F_q(t)$ generated by the $n$-th iterates of $f$ for any $n \geq 1$. As a secondary result, we determine the asymptotic distribution of these degrees for arbitrary generic $f$. Specifically, in the limit as $n$ approaches infinity, the relative frequencies of each degree converge to a well-defined limit vector whose components are explicitly calculable.

We calculate one-loop contributions to $\sigma(e^+ e^- \to Zh)$ from several benchmark extension of the Standard Model scalar sectors. Using a general two-Higgs-doublet framework, we determine how $\sigma$ is affected by new physics in $\sigma(e^+ e^- \to Zh)$ within specific scenarios: the Simplified Susy Model (BSM), the Simplified Single Scale Model (SSM), and variations of the SSM characterized by different mass spectra. Our study reveals that, contrary to tree-level expectations where $\sigma$ solely depends on Higgs quartic couplings, one-loop corrections are sensitive to the full set of parameters defining the model. Furthermore, we demonstrate that even though validity ranges for specific BSM interpretations may be narrow, the resulting deviations in measured cross-sections can be substantial and experimentally observable.

Saturn's stratosphere near its poles is characterized by large, warm vortices and sharp seasonal shifts in atmospheric trace gases, phenomena that are driven by substantial solar and radiative changes depending on the season. The rate of vertical radiative relaxation in this region is rapid enough to capture these seasonal variations, yet it is too slow to account for the rapid horizontal migration of sulfur dioxide observed in the stratosphere and mesosphere. The study presents a simple model indicating that vertical transport—driven by either mechanical turbulence or buoyancy-driven processes—accounts for SO2 concentration profiles throughout Saturn's stratosphere and lower mesosphere. The research further demonstrates that the magnitude of this transport is consistent with theoretical estimates involving stratospheric vortex dynamics and wave breaking. Consequently, radiative heating and vertical mixing jointly regulate the thermal and chemical structure of the polar stratosphere and lower mesosphere on seasonal timescales, whereas horizontal diffusion is insufficient to explain the observed SO2 variations.

This paper examines a mass-supercritical focusing nonlinearity within the Schrödinger equation, defined outside a smooth, bounded obstacle in $\R^{d}$ subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions. We demonstrate that negative energy solutions exhibit finite-time blow-up. Additionally, under energy subcritical assumptions and specific symmetry constraints, we establish a blow-up criteria based on optimal ground states consistent with Holmer and Roudenko's previous results for $\R^{d}$, albeit here in the presence of an obstacle and under distinct nonlinearity and setup requirements. A significant innovation is the derivation of a new, coherent Lyapunov functional applicable to holomorphic flows that cannot easily be reduced to their real-time counterparts. Lastly, we analyze the holographic case where these solutions face a finite-time singularity, with their asymptotic profiles governed by a reduced ordinary differential system of finite dimension.

Surface termination plays a pivotal role in determining the physical properties of materials, a concept that is especially critical for doctral systems. In this study, we examine the influence of surface termination on the metal-insulator transition (MIT) in V$_2$O$_3$ using first-principles calculations. We identify three distinct surface terminations for the monoclinic system of V$_2$O$_3$: the stoichiometric top surface (T), the vacancy-rich surface (V), and an intermediate variant (I). Our results reveal that the MIT in V$_2$O$_3$ is highly sensitive to these different terminations. While the T and I terminations inherently exhibit metallic character, the V termination acts as a semiconductor. The electronic band structure analysis indicates that the band gap for the V state arises from the absence of bands near the Fermi level, primarily due to hybridization between O $2p$ and V $3d$ orbitals. Furthermore, comparing the bond lengths across terminations shows bond-order alternation, serving as an additional indicator of the V state's semiconducting behavior. Finally, we assessed the stability of each surface state using both total energy methods and bond-order parameters. Ultimately, our findings demonstrate that the V-state's semiconducting nature is robust against various defects and adatom incorporations, highlighting how surface termination serves as a decisive factor in this phenomenon.

We document experimental observations from a collision between two dark solitons in a one-dimensional Lieb-Lattice, whose positions and movements are governed by quantum mechanics. This collision serves as a visible indicator of a underlying quasi-Bose-Einstein condensation occurring at the lattice sites, which in turn drives the movement and posiitonding dynamics of the solitons. We demonstrate how the collision can be used to measure the onsite correlations and offer an explanation for a previously puzzling increase in soliton width post-collision, attributing it to the post-interaction presence of vortices in the soliton's internal structure. Finally, we utilize this event as a practical method to detect and visualize quasi-Bose-Einstein condensation within systems that exhibit soliton dynamics.

We construct the complete linearisation functor, which associates with every $k$-graded bundle—a specific type of structured graded manifold—a $k$-fold vector bundle. We provide a full characterization of this functor's image, establishing it as a subcategory of $k$-fold vector bundles; these bundles consist of symmetric structures endowed with an indexed family of morphisms from the symmetric group $\mathbb{S}_k$. Notably, regardless of the underlying graded bundle $E$, its complete linearisation yields a canonical section of the total space functor (the bundle projection), an observation we describe and analyse. Finally, we take the functorial approach to identification, examining how the complete linearisation behaves under various linearisation functors derived by other researchers.

The classical definition of Tamagawa numbers for algebraic tori, initially based on orbital integrals by Godement, requires reynolds functions within a minimal Moinesque (Moy-Prasad) structure. In this paper, I develop a new definition of these numbers using the same framework but focusing on the totally Hilbertian case. I demonstrate that when restricted to finite fields, these counts align with Godement's original theory. As an application, these results provide a reformulation and proof of the fundamental equality of Tamagawa numbers.

Spectroscopy relies on the interplay between light and matter to reveal details about a sample's microscopic composition, often necessitating interferometric methods for full characterization of the emergent light field. However, current techniques for detecting phase shifts in this phase amplitude are frequently too cumbersome for practical application. We introduce a deep learning-based tool designed to extract phase information from straightforward, non-interferometric spectroscopic data. We validate this approach through mode decomposition testing within a single resonator and chemical analysis within a sensing cuvette, demonstrating its robust analytical potential. Additionally, we provide general guidance for integrating phase-less data analysis across various spectroscopic applications.

Mapping classical disordered statistical mechanics models to quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes serves as a highly effective technique for evaluating the intrinsic noise resilience and critical thresholds of these codes against phenomenological noise. This paper broadens the scope of such mappings to incorporate realistic, multi-correlated quantum error processes. We demonstrate that these intertwined noise sources correspond to a family of coupled Ising glasses, where the coupling constants are determined directly by the logical operator structure of the Heisenberg-42 code. Leveraging this framework allows us to construct noise phase diagrams that identify fundamental physical limits inherent to the code, attributes that cannot be gleaned solely from simulation of the QEC circuit under noise. Furthermore, our analysis reveals a specific subclass of codes wherein noise disorder is beneficial, enabling performance beyond the limits achievable with only phenomenological noise.

We address the Darcy flow dynamics within a fractured, porous environment by formulating a mixed Hilbert space formulation of the Mixed Finite Element Method (MFEM). The fracture network is distinguished into two categories: conductive fractures, which permit smooth continuity of both mixed finite element variables across the fracture surfaces, and blocking fractures, which impede the permeation of both variables across their extents. The formulation derives the convergence of the numerical formulation in terms of mesh parameters. Furthermore, the feasibility of the proposed MFEM in accurately simulating fracture flows at complex fracture networks that include large aperture fractures is demonstrated through numerical experiments.

We present a detailed investigation into a superconducting spin-triplet valve composed of two parallel ferromagnetic (FM) layers separated by a superconducting (SC) layer, focusing on a configuration where the left FM layer exhibits uniform magnetization and the system as a whole possesses nonuniform magnetic order. In this setup, the difference between the precession planes of the asymptotic exchange fields in the two configurations defines an effective exchange anisotropy. Within the diffusive regime, the triplet components of the superconducting phase are categorized into those parallel and antipariper to this effective exchange anisotropy. The triplet components parallel to the anisotropy experience either significant suppression or complete elimination, whereas those antiparallel experience the longest possible suppression. Consequently, the nonuniform magnetic order induces a specific type of triplet superconductivity characterized by out-of-plane spin components. Ultimately, the proximity-induced magnetization electric current induces a longitudinal superconducting spin current that selectively suppresses specific triplet channels to enhance long-range triplet correlations.

Hypathese testing is a fundamental activity across statistics, research, and statistics-related disciplines. When comparing two hypotheses, practitioners often employ p-values to assess support for one against the other; however, p-values have significant drawbacks and are increasingly being replaced by Bayes factors. A Bayes factor quantifies the evidence regarding one hypothesis relative to another. Unfortunately, estimating a Bayes factor typically requires intractable integrals. Historically, Monte Carlo techniques for approximating these factors were constrained by the necessity that probability distributions under both hypotheses possess overlapping support. This paper demonstrates that Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods can successfully compute Bayes factors even when support overlap is absent.

Discourse markers function as "glue" connecting sentences and paragraphs, signaling the pragmatic or structural nature of ensuing linguistic units; however, their variability across languages and contexts poses challenges for automatic recognition. Since these markers frequently indicate specific relationships—such as concession when markers like "but" appear—their identification serves as a vital step in discourse analysis and various Natural Language Processing tasks. This paper introduces a new semantic discourse marker dataset built using the Wikipedia English corpus and an OpenIE-based extraction algorithm. We further evaluate top-performing "Transformers" architectures and derive significant insights, demonstrating that despite markers being non-generative and conditionable on context, state-of-the-art models achieve acceptable results without additional hand-crafted features or human annotations, despite dealing with underseen words due to the dataset's open-vocabulary character.

Utilizing optical detection of the vacancy defect's electronic state, our study examines how temperature and extreme high temperature vacuum influences the spin-dependent luminescence of the vacancy defect. As temperature elevates, the spin-dependent luminescence signal diminishes linearly with temperature.

Substitution to luminescent spectral measurements reveals a shift in the spectral peak frequency of the luminescence spectrum that increases linearly with temperature, attributed the lattice expansion of diamond lattice expansion responsible for the linear thermal expansion coefficient. Additionally, the fine and hyperfine structures within the luminescence spectrum, including those arising from interaction with two-level systems in the local environment are preserved with increasing temperature.

Calculations indicate the thermal relaxation lifetime of this quantum state is approximately 1.3 microseconds. Utilizing the hyperfine splitting structure associated with the vacancy defect's electronic state, magnetometry remains viable and functions dependably in this extreme thermal vacuum setting. Finally, observations indicate that the vacancy defect serves as an ideal model system for analyzing the mechanisms underlying radiation emission under these specific high-temperature, high-vacuum experimental conditions.

Although the backpropagation algorithm is essential for training artificial neural networks, its requirement for weight sharing makes it implausible as a biological model. In response, this paper introduces, specifically using a two-layer context, a training method that circumvents this limitation by omitting explicit error calculation and the backpropagation process altogether. Additionally, we introduce a distinct error metric tailored for offline language learning. Initial simulations indicate that this approach is feasible, while theoretical bounds on the outer product error suggest it may scale in a manner similar to brain energy usage.

A strong edge-coloring of a graph $G$ involves edge coloring it such that every clique of size at least 2 has distinct associated colors. In this context, any clique treated as a set of incident edges functions as a "superedge," implying that all its members must carry unique colors. Consequently, the rate of strong edge coloring never exceeds the size of the largest possible chromatic number for $G$'s line. For diverse classes of graphs exhibiting specific structural attributes, we introduce and analyze various bounded-rates strong edge colorings tailored to trees and graphs possessing bounded diameter. We further present concepts, definitions, and theoretical results regarding coloring graphs with limited diameter.

This paper focuses on integers $q \ge 3$, where $\chi$ is a Dirichlet character modulo $q$ and $L(s, \chi)$ denotes the associated Dirichlet $L$-functions. By employing standard techniques from complex analysis and the theory of differential equations involving Fuchsian equations, we derive several properties of these functions that arise from their connections to such differential equations. Specifically, we analyze the zeros of $L(1/2+it, \chi)$ for $t \in \mathbb{R}$ within the critical strip. Furthermore, we investigate the behavior of these zeros near the critical line, examining the gaps between consecutive zeros. Our results offer precise estimates and statistical insights regarding the lengths of intervals between consecutive zeros, supplemented by graphical visualizations of their observed distributions.

Heavy particles accessible at high-energy colliders produce distinct signatures at gravitational wave detectors through resonant production and subsequent decay. Specifically, the sharp peaks associated with the collider's resonance in gravitational waves are flanked by distinct steps caused by the continuum background; the amplitude of these steps scales directly with the square of the coupling constants of the heavy particles. We present methodology for discerning these resonances from stochastic noise within observed data, utilizing both full collider cross-section information and partial data derived from heavy-flavor-tagged jet selections. Furthermore, we establish complementary relationships between projected exclusion limits or discovery sensitivities for such particles at future high-energy colliders and generic stochastic noise limits of next-generation high-energy probes searching for deviations in the Planck scale. Our analysis demonstrates detectability or robust constraining capabilities for Third Generation (3G) detectors covering mass ranges relevant to colliders up to several TeV. Notably, the sensitivity of 3G probes to these spectral features complements traditional searches focused on high-mass bumps, potentially offering superior performance in specific theoretical scenarios.

This study examines force-driven, rigid helical microorganisms in both Newtonian and viscoelastic (Boger) environments, manipulating parameters such as the size of both the main body and helical tail (relative to the fluid's relaxation time), the elasticity, and the viscous stress. The findings indicate that Newtonian and responses from viscoelastic experiences can be entirely decoupled through strategic adjustment of the geometry. While Newtonian motion is constrained by specific physical limits, these microorganisms can exhibit broad ranges of behavior in viscoelastic conditions. Notably, the capacity for propulsion in these complex fluids depends on a regime that allows either enhanced or suppressed speeds relative to Newtonian baseline, leading to a triad of outcomes where viscoelasticity either accelerates, decelerates, or leaves the swimming speed unchanged compared to Newtonian fluid dynamics.

We introduce a novel social learning framework where agents engage in a normal-form game and learn through a voting-based externalities mechanism. In this setup, each agent selects an action suggested by a fixed set of peers; if a majority of suggestions align, the agent adopts the majority action. The core inquiry examines convergence patterns when individuals are bound by these rigid social connections while comparing individual learning methods versus various forms of social learning within game-theoretic contexts. Theoretical findings reveal that while non-cooperative learning algorithms typically converge to a no-regret equilibrium state, social learning dynamics often stall at cyclic behaviors failing to reach a Nash Equilibrium (NE). To validate this theory empirically, we employ extensive simulations across extensive game instances, offering further evidence. Conversely, under specific learning rules NEs are attained; furthermore, we analyze the speed of convergence relative to scenarios without externalities. The results indicate that although social learning may cycle or converge slowly, NEs are ultimately achieved and converge faster than those in individual learning environments, frequently landing near the Pareto frontier of feasible outcomes.

Information security within cyberspace relies heavily on security measures, with the National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Network (NCIIPN) serving as a core focus. Effectively managing security across this extensive network of measures is a significant challenge. Ontology-driven approaches offer a viable solution, yet existing research often employs generic terms like "security measures" or "events" without precision, leaving specific frameworks unaddressed. These vague terminology gaps hinder current methods from optimizing the efficient administration of NCIIPN security. This study introduces a dedicated NCIIPN Security Ontology (NCISO) framework designed to resolve these unresolved issues and facilitate better governance of national critical infrastructures. Built upon W3C standards, the framework was constructed using the OWL ontology language via the Protégé tool, ensuring interoperability. Population for reasoning was achieved using the Pellet reasoner, allowing the system to derive inferences and verify consistency effectively. This structured approach lays the groundwork for advanced information security management capabilities, specifically enhancing measure of similarity search and improved decision-making support for NCIIPN operations.

The opinion dynamics model represents a significant branch of statistical physics dedicated to understanding collective behavior. Within this field, the Ising agent model stands out due to its capacity to capture both conformist and anti-conformist tendencies. In the present work, we analyze the opionion dynamics of an conformist/anti-conformist hybrid system driven by homophily (attraction to like opinions) and the tendency to follow the majority. Our approach employs the Edwards Anderson spin-glass technique, utilizing an mean-field framework where mean-field approximations treat opinion vectors. Within this model formulation, a unique opinion state involves the coexistence of distinct opinion values separated by a discrete gap. While system parameters control the final level of polarization, specific threshold values are identified that trigger the abrupt emergence of strong, clonal opinion structures analogous to spontaneous breaking of symmetry in standard magnetization processes. Further investigation reveals that the macroscopic macro of final opinion states, characterized by this macroscopic polarization and the distribution of its magnitudes, varies dramatically depending on the concentration of anti-conformist agents. We ultimately establish a clear connection between the proportion of anti-conformist participants and the emergence of robust ferromagnetic ordering within the agent collective.

The transmission of coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 occurs primarily through respiratory droplets and aerosols. Since these droplets evaporate quickly in ambient conditions, altering their diameter, mass, and viral concentration, understanding and modeling this evaporation are crucial. Although a previous study offered an analytical two-stage model for droplet evolution (where Stage 1 involves cooling to ambient temperature and Stage 2 involves constant-flux evaporation until reaching thermal equilibrium), that initial framework did not account for energy exchanges between droplets and the environment. This research introduces an enhanced version of the two-stage model that incorporates such environmental heat transfer dynamics into the mathematical formulation. The revised approach provides non-inverting closed-form solutions for radius and temperature evolution, with the first-stage formulas updated to reflect the new heating/cool considerations. Furthermore, the original constant-flux assumption for the second stage is substituted with a more realistic variable-flux model. While these enhancements yield only marginal quantitative differences under most scenarios, the improved model is significantly robust for epidemiological predictions. Finally, the updated framework is utilized to analyze the evolution of SARS-CoV-2 within droplets.

Neural networks are profoundly reshaping scientific discovery, yet they often struggle to provide absolute certainty in their outputs. This represents a significant hurdle in assessing the reliability of AI-assisted science, as it necessitates that models not only learn accurate mappings from training data but also quantify uncertainty alongside them. Uncertainty in deep learning generally breaks down into two categories: aleatoric (inherent stochasticity in individual samples) and structural (systematic limitations of the network architecture itself). Although various methods address each type separately, they frequently fail to capture both effectively, particularly within the context of efficiency and reliability-critical domains like high-energy physics. This paper surveys uncertainty estimation strategies specifically for neural network acceleration techniques such as Fixed and Dynamic Quantization, as well as Stochastic Neural Networks. It examines how these approaches manifest and are handled aleatoric and structural uncertainties. Furthermore, it highlights significant gaps in current research and suggests promising avenues for future investigation.

We demonstrate that for a specified class of oriented trees $\mathcal{D}$, the ordinary and symbolic powers of this ideal are always equivalent. Furthermore, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions ensuring the equality between these powers specifically for lines equipped with their natural orientations.
We examine the one-piaulet unitary matrix model under finite dimensions $ N $, employing exact partition function expressions for both $\text{SU}( N )$ and $\text{ U }( N )$ symmetries.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are now integral to many safety-critical computer vision tasks, such as autonomous driving. Although clipping techniques like activation dropout and activation saturation have been studied as noise filters for general applications, these same mechanisms offer a pathway to introduce reliable noise specifically for systems where reliability is paramount. This paper investigates the feasibility of employing activation clipping to inject stochastic disturbances into CNNs, with the specific aim of enhancing noise resilience. To support this research, we introduce and apply Activation Saturation (AS), a novel saturation mechanism. Furthermore, we develop a methodology to transform this approach into noise, allowing for noise simulation and analysis. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that these techniques effectively filter noise, enabling accurate detection of noise images, and also provide robust protection against adversarial examples.

The European Central Bank's definition of clearing or netting significantly influences a nation's economy by shaping corporate transactions and interactions. Briefly, netting offers an alternative to standard inter-company payment processes; it functions as an agreement where mutual debts are offset and the payment obligations of two or more parties are converted into direct settlements based on their respective balances. This paper introduces a suite of graph algorithms designed to provide optimal netting solutions on the scale of a countrywide economy, calculating results with computational efficiency. Tested using invoice data from the Romanian Ministry of Economy, our findings demonstrate that classic graph algorithms remain effective in addressing critical financial infrastructure concerns.

This study offers an explicit extension of the $r$-symmetrized Jordanian twist developed by Giaquinto and Zhang and verifies that this generalization meets the 2-cocycle requirement. We introduce closed-form equations for both the related twisted coproduct and star product. Finally, it is demonstrated that our extension matches the result derived from the simple Jordanian twist via twisting using a 1-cochain.

We propose a multilingual common semantic space grounded in distributional semantics, enabling knowledge and resource sharing by projecting vocabulary from various languages into an integrated representation space that exceeds basic word-level semantics to include phrase and sentence levels. To achieve this semantic embedding space, clustering is performed using three distinct signals: word clusters based on co-contexts, co-text cluster-based word clusters, clusters of syntactically co-parsed sentences. Relative co-text cluster prototypes are established as the co-text co-cluster words' central axis, establishing words' relative positions within the cluster and thus defining their meanings. Relative co-cluster words are introduced to represent words from different languages that are embedded near identical regional areas within the common semantic space.

Recent research indicates that pre-trained language models achieve exceptional performance on few-shot natural language understanding benchmarks, largely because these methods depend heavily on the vast scale of their training data for success. Conversely, dialogue state tracking (DST) relies on numerous complex and often overlapping dialogue attributes, making the application of existing few-shot approaches limited by their requirement for extensive training samples. In this paper, we present ASSIST, a framework tailored to few-shot learning for dialogue state tracking that functions effectively even with minimal training data. The core innovation of ASSIST is the use of prototype vectors to represent dialogue templates. Specifically, for each attribute, the system converts an attribute-value pair into an embedding, then aggregates these into a single prototype vector serving as a representative for that specific attribute template. In the latter half of October 2019, widespread violence sweeping through Chile was triggered by dissenting tuition policies and rapidly escalated into a nationwide general insurrection. This study analyzes the spatial distribution of the rioting in the Santiago Metropolitan area. The spatial activity pattern of the rioting adheres primarily to the friction gradient non stationary cellular automata (FNCAs) model, with the non-stationary cellular automata (SCA) model serving as a secondary influence. The primary friction gradient factor is the presence of urban infrastructure, specifically roads, while administrative boundaries play the most significant role in determining friction within the SCA component. Insights derived from this analysis of spatial riot dynamics can aid law enforcement in enhancing their capacity to predict and mitigate future unrest.

By leveraging the Atacama Large Millimeter/subarray Telescope (ALMA), we have detected the Br$\gamma$ hydrogen recombination line in the star-forming galaxy M82 centered on its nucleus. Our observations reveal the line's central velocity and width while demonstrating that the peak intensity source is confined to a 0".17 region (equivalent to 0.016 parsec at M82's distance), or roughly half the radius of a massive OB association. Representing the first direct detection of such a line in a galaxy by TATL (Atacama Large Millimeter Array), our findings offer crucial insights into the formation processes of Br$\gamma$ and illustrate the ATAM Large Millimeter/subarray Array's capability to observe stars rates via this method. Additionally, our analysis indicates that any connection between Br$\gamma$ width and HII region ionizing photon emission from core stellar populations is likely broken during the transition from Br$\gamma$ HII region to super-wind. Finally, our results regarding star formation rate accuracy highlight potential accuracy issues associated with using fundamental constants and recombination coefficients in the standard calculation formula alongside the refined central source size.

Our work examines the boundary separating the cone of sum-of-squares (SOS) real polynomials from the cone of nonnegative real polynomials. While the SOC is contained within the nonnegative cone and they coincide only for specific cases, recent findings by Blekherman suggest that, with an appropriate measure, the boundary exhibits fractal characteristics. This study investigates the geometric properties of this boundary while treating it as a manifold to understand its structure within the context of polynomial theory.

When high-scale physics features a heavy lepton sector, the low-energy effective theory exhibits non-unitary behavior in the mixing matrix. This study investigates both indirect constraints (from observable deviations) and direct constraints (from new physics searches) on specific matrix elements under the assumption of such high-scale heavy leptons. We observe that, due to established indirect bounds reflecting current non-unitarity limits, only three matrix elements remain accessible to direct detection; furthermore, two of these involve rows or columns of the mixing matrix exclusively subject to negligible indirect limits. Additionally, employing a generic global analysis of experimental data, we determine a preferred structure for the deformation of unitarity within this matrix.

Containment checking for regular expressions (REs) represents a fundamental challenge with wide-ranging applications, typically framed as determining if $L(r_1) \subseteq L(r_2)$ for two REs $r_1$ and $r_2$, under the assumption that both define languages over the same alphabet. A critical obstacle is the "subset problem," where $L(r_1) \cap L(r_2)$ contains only a subset of $L(r_1)$. While deciding containment for basic REs remains feasible despite a cubic complexity cost relative to expression size, this complexity escalates dramatically when dealing with extended regular expressions (which include the subset operator) due to potentially exponential expression growth during standard processing methods like translation to alternating finite automata (AFA). Although we can efficiently construct direct non-deterministic REs that represent the intersection of two such expressions—essential for containment verification by complementing $r_2$—these expressions may still be exponentially larger than the originals. Fortunately, effective techniques exist to directly construct compact (polynomial-sized) $\varepsilon$-NFA for the intersection of two such expressions, forming the basis of our proposed algorithm, which efficiently solves the containment problem for normal and extended REs of comparable lengths.

Precise and resilient localization represents a critical requirement for autonomous mobile entities. Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) methods utilize data from cameras and inertial units to determine position and orientation, and recent deep learning approaches to VIO have garnered significant attention due to their ability to deliver location estimates at high speed with minimal latency, thereby supporting tasks such as visual regression and human-computer interaction. However, these state-of-the-art models often demand substantial computational resources, posing challenges for mobile agents that seek to deploy multiple instances for visual localization and recruit inertial fusion techniques for enhanced perception. Our introduction of the "LightGlue" model and the "X-INS" predictor network successfully addresses this efficiency bottleneck; LightGlue operates with a lightweight architecture enabling real-time inference on mobile graphics processing units, while X-INS extracts essential inertial features from reduced fusion inputs using a streamlined design. Our evaluation indicates that S. Lightglue demonstrates superior performance compared to existing methods on both synthetic and real-world benchmarks, effectively providing high-precision, feature-based visual-to-visual correspondences. Complementarily, X-INS delivers accurate attitude prediction using only basic inertial data, supporting robust multi-agent localization when integrated with VIO frameworks.

Quantum mechanics relies fundamentally on linear algebra, yet emerging research explores how systems can exhibit beneficial behaviors by utilizing nonlinear operators within a quantum context. This study presents the square-root (n^2) model, a theoretical framework built on a nonlinear operator, which turns out to be an equivalent description of a higher-order type-W WyIeI semimetre in three dimensions. Interestingly, this (n^2) model produces no isolated bulk hayalls, nonetheless exhibits a pair of star-shaped electrons known as hyperbolic states, located in internally interfaces formed between two different nonlinear trimers. Additionally, this model demonstrates narrowed down to two dimensions, yields a promising application towards building quantum compute technologies using its neutral atoms systems.

This article examines a data completion problem for time-harmonic Maxwell equations regarding the electric field within a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$. The objective is to reconstruct missing components of the electric field inside $\Omega$, using the known components and other field properties, subject to specific constraints preventing trivial solutions. To this end, a quasi-reversibility approach is proposed and analyzed. The study establishes the existence and uniqueness of solutions for the proposed problem alongside their convergence. Finally, numerical simulations are presented to validate the methodology's efficacy.

In this work, we investigate Federated Selective Aggregation (FedSA), an approach designed to train a student model for a specific target domain by integrating contributions from multiple teachers varied in both origin and quality. This method chooses and weights input features from these diverse teacher networks rather than simply averaging their global parameters. To implement this selection, we create two weighting strategies: one based on how well a teacher aligns with the student on the specific domain and the other on the intrinsic value of that teacher's contributions. Demonstration of effectiveness across four datasets spanning six domains confirms that focusing learning on a single aggregated teacher is insufficient for targeting particular domains and indicates that FedSA delivers significant performance gains over current state-of-the-art federated transfer learning benchmarks.

Grid cells, discovered roughly ten years ago in the rat's medial entorhinal cortex, display firing patterns tied to periodic locations in their surroundings. These unique traits led to early theories proposing that such cells furnish a metric for spatial representation. Later studies revealed numerous insights regarding the attributes of grid cells and their surrounding neural circuits within the parahippocampal-hippocampal area, necessitating updates to previous models. This review article intends to comprehensively survey grid cell research from an environmental perspective. It examines specific aspects including phase offsets, phase precession, firing under stationary and head-fixed conditions, the influence of sensory inputs, and how cellular individuality shapes their function.

Using recent 3D global hydrodynamic simulations of non-magnetic, convective Sun proxies, we investigate how magnetic fields influence the onset and dynamics of dynamos. Specifically, we examine systems where magnetic self-excitation is impossible due to high Rossby numbers or instability, yet external forces (like tidal interactions) seed fields that evolve. These low-Reynolds-number (in terms of rotation) systems produce dynamics dominated by magnetic evolution under external constraint. We evaluated multiple initial magnetic configurations across varying degrees of convective turbulence to model their time-dependent behavior.

Our primary findings indicate that weak to moderate external seeding allows solar-type stars to develop complex, subtapedil dynamos operating out of magnetic steady-state due to take a long time to decay or adjust as rotation dominates. These systems sustain dynamo action well into parameter regimes dominated by convolution, generating $\gamma$-index reversed field and magnetohydrodynamic feedback loops that profoundly impact stellar activity cycles and physics beyond simple auto-excitation models.

The quantum null energy condition (QNEC) establishes a lower bound on the energy-momentum tensor, correlating it with the acceleration of quantum entanglement. While existing proofs rely on the state's two-point function satisfying the optical and Penrose inequalities—properties not guaranteed within quantum field theory—we demonstrate that the QNEC holds by two distinct mechanisms: first, if the short-distance singularity structure of the two-point function adheres to Landau's principle of minimal entropy, the condition is satisfied; second, if the two-point function exhibits power-law behavior consistent with conformal symmetry at short ranges, the QNEC also applies. Both mechanisms validate across both Euclidean and Minkowski spacetime formulations. Furthermore, when applied to quantum states in de Sitter space characterized by conformal symmetry at small scales, this result provides geometric insight into why the quantum null energy condition is universally satisfied.

(TDM) $q$-relative entropy to assess how unitary dynamics in a two-level system accelerates or delays the emergence of distinguishability between initial and evolved states. Our analysis reveals that while the existence of specific monotone pairs guarantees either early or late divergence (a signature of accelerationist, retrograde behavior) for any initial state and evolution path, no single TDM-based asymmetry monotone universally identifies these patterns across all scenarios. Furthermore, by utilizing the geometric nature of the TDM $q$-relative entropy, we establish a direct method to determine the distinguishability time itself, demonstrating this approach through qubit models illustrating both predicted acceleration and its delay.

Superconducting quantum circuits are recognized as a foremost platform for realizing quantum computation via fixed architecture methods, yet the effectiveness of high-coherence two-qubit gates via photon displacement remains unverified. To investigate limitations arising from trajectory control within this system, the study employs a quantum model accounting for realistic path irregularities in computing modules with five levels of degeneracy. Analyzing the specific case of a phase-loop voltage setting, the work demonstrates how intrinsic material flaws can undermine fidelity even when coherence is typically strong, provided the choice of operational trajectories lacks model accuracy. The study further investigates the benefits of enhancing model fidelity and the impact of calibrating loop phases manually instead of relying on theoretical predictions implicitly.

This paper investigates twisted algebraic $K$-theory within a motivic context. For a smooth variety $X$ over a field of zero characteristic and an Azumaya algebra $\mathcal{A}$ on $X$, we construct a $\mathcal{A}$-twisted motivic spectral sequence. This construction involves determining the slices of the twisted algebraic motivic $K$-theory spectrum, treating them as twisted variants of motivic cohomology. Our approach leverages the invariance of these constructions under étale covers and employs comparison theorems to establish results specifically for locally constant twisted terms. Additionally, we demonstrate the existence of an external Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence operating within the realm of twisted algebraic $K$-motivic theory. Furthermore, related connections are explored between the input data, the resulting spectral sequence limits, and the associated twisted extension groups.

Dynamics of suspended liquid droplets represent an essential aspect of interfacial physics with significant industrial applications ranging from pharmaceuticals to fine chemicals and petroleum. Within chemistry and physics curricula, understanding droplet transport, migration, and evaporation is typically introduced early; however, an evaporating droplet surrounded by three immiscible fluids presents a more intricate scenario often reserved for advanced study. This system serves as a fundamental model for evaluating chemical and interfacial physics principles while addressing pervasive industrial relevance. Consequently, I present a conceptual framework detailing the behaviors of a droplet under general conditions, focusing on its model system of evaporation within a superfluid environment. By analyzing this model, one can derive predictive insights applicable to a wide array of more complex liquid systems.

Recent breakthroughs in hardware for evaluating tensor network (TN) representations of quantum states have significantly scaled up from small, trivial examples to substantial systems. This manuscript surveys the innovations driving this period of rapid advancement, highlighting key new real-space algorithms, pivotal metrics for assessing TN performance, and cutting-edge computational results. Together, these developments demonstrate the capacity to generate and manipulate on a larger variety of promising states a wide array of significant states crucial for future quantum computing endeavors.

Accurate tissue characterization is essential for understanding both the anatomical integrity and physiological roles of healthy organs, as well as diagnosing cancer and related disorders. Deep-learning methodologies have recently shown significant potential in automating the segmentation and classification of cellular and histological features within histopathological images to facilitate these characterizations. However, effectively integrating such cell- and tissue-level features into clinical decision-support systems requires modeling the semantic hierarchy inherent in cellular identities and their pathologies—a demand that aligns perfectly with Variational Autoencoder (VAE) architectures capable of learning compact latent representations through a hierarchical lens. Consequently, this study introduces a novel bidirectional VAE designed specifically for cell- and tissue-level deep pathology characterization. Concretely, this approach employs Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) modules within both the encoder and decoder of the VAE to establish a hierarchical framework that integrates discrete cells with tissue-level semantics connotatively. Furthermore, this study validates its proposed technique using two distinct datasets derived from both the Cancer Research Center Foundation (CRIF) and the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Results demonstrate notable advancements in distinguishing cellular phenotypes and tissue categories relative to baseline models, affirming the practicality of such semantic hierarchical representations for enhancing deep pathology analysis within clinical contexts.

Multivariate point processes are extensively used to analyze events characterized by type, such as neural firing patterns, financial dealings, digital communications, or ecological disasters. Among these, the Hawkes process stands as a prominent model where an event's likelihood is influenced—either enhancing or inhibiting subsequent activity—by past occurrences. This paper introduces a flexible Bayesian nonparametric framework designed specifically for process-thinned data, aggregating multiple underlying processes. Within this setting, we introduce the Bayesian density regression model for the thinning functions and employ the Chinese Dirichlet Process to address the infinite-dimensional parameter space inherent in these functions. Additionally, we propose an efficient sampling-based inference algorithm capable of estimating parameters for the Hawkes process model using only data related to event timestamps. Effectiveness of this proposed method is demonstrated through simulations and a practical application analyzing volcanic eruption and seismic activity records, providing insight into the complex spatiotemporal interactions between the Fort Hood shooting incident and fluctuations in financial markets.

Smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) is celebrated for maintaining highly accurate conservation properties, making it the gold standard for methods that explicitly enforce such constraints. Nevertheless, approaches that strictly conserve angular momentum and entropy alongside SPH's native mass and energy conservation remain scarce. This study introduces a novel formulation of SPH that achieves exact simultaneous conservation of angular momentum, mass, energy, and entropy. Furthermore, we derive the associated numerical gradients and verify the scheme's validity using one- and three-dimensional shock tube tests, as well as black hole accretion simulations involving both smooth test fluids and multi-black-hole scenarios.

Although Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based medical image segmentation has achieved remarkable advances, it typically demands extensive manual annotations. Given that storing and transmitting large medical imaging files often poses significant privacy risks and infrastructure challenges, semi-supervised learning approaches that rely on small labeled and larger unlabeled datasets offer a promising solution. Nevertheless, using deep learning models for this purpose in the medical domain is frequently hindered by prohibitive memory consumption. Addressing this, we demonstrate, through both empirical testing and theoretical derivation, that employing data sampling strategies to collect representative image patches from the dataset is an effective way to enhance segmentation accuracy. Leveraging the equivalence between segmentation on whole volumes and segmentation on sampled patches within a unified framework, our findings indicate that training on a training set augmented by sampled patches constitutes a powerful form of data enhancement. Crucially, this strategy not only boosts segmentation metrics but can also replace full-volume training entirely with a hybrid approach using training and sampled data. Importantly, implementing these techniques with sampled patches leads to efficiency gains: the approach requires storing only the training set and samples, drastically reducing memory requirements while maintaining, if not surpassing, performance compared to training on complete volumes. Our approach, designated as Quasi-SSL (Q-SSL), achieves, if not surpasses, comparable or superior metrics to standard semi-supervised methods. Additionally, because Q-SSL training using data sampling requires significantly less storage capacity, it is more accessible and efficient.

The 1.5-order formalism serves as an essential tool in the quantization of supergravity and related theories, such as Witten's cubic gravity. This paper identifies the foundational limitation of the 1.5-order method by demonstrating that its definition of the Hilbert space measure is incompatible with the positive-definiteness required for a consistent time-component. We present an alternative first-order framework grounded in a new, coherent interpretation of the reality conditions specific to supergravity and Witten's cubic gravity. This proposed scheme not only streamlines the formalism but also establishes a more robust foundation for analyzing these theories, including investigations into potential issues with unitarity in Witten's cubic gravity.

Conventional solid-state optical materials face spatial limitations, prompting this study to propose a plasma-based waveplate utilizing the magnetic field gradient of an asymmetric electron cyclotron resonance structure to transform linearly polarized light into circularly polarized light at nearly 100% efficiency. The proposed design features a single plate with a working area of 1.5 cm², where the transformation is localized within a 5 mm radius. The field gradient drives this design, requiring minimal investment in spatial accuracy and incurring no spatial restrictions associated with larger systems. Spatial testing confirms that the field gradient is stable over time and that the optical functionality is reproducible across multiple plates. Energy and momentum balance analysis supports these findings, while three-dimensional numerical simulations align closely with the measured data. Comparisons with existing spatially localized optical components suggest this plasma waveplate offers a compact solution that can be integrated into laser systems operating at higher photon energies.

This study re-examines the search for a nonzero tau-lepton electric dipole moment (EDM), focusing on $e^+e^- \to \tau^+\tau^-$ annihilation data from the BaBar collaboration at PEP-II. We detail a systematic analysis of perturbative and non-perturbative properties of the one-loop effective $\gamma$-tau tau vertex, specifically highlighting signatures of an imaginary part in the tau tau gamma vertex related to the tau lepton's electric dipole form factor. In the situation where the embedded hadron sector exhibits a tau lepton pair with an effective dipole moment that would produce a characteristic asymmetry linearly proportional to the center-of-mass energy and form factor, we find the sensitivity for the form factor is $10^{-4}$ in case both the hadrons decay semihadronically to approximately $2\times 10^{-5}$ when one of the hadrons decays semileptonically. If the energy is increased to higher values such as those of higher luminosity or even to leptonic final states with higher precision, this could offer a more precise probe into new physics beyond the Standard Model. Using these methodologies and projections, we suggest future studies focusing on the energy dependence of the form factor, the magnitude of which could be used to constrain the form factor further and potentially infer information about new physics if such anomalies persist into higher energy regimes where form factors become significant.

This section examines the decoding of rank metric codes under the assumption that error matrices are symmetric, demonstrating two key findings.

### 1. Sufficient Conditions for Rank and Half-Packing Distance
First off, we establish that these codes can correct any symmetric error pattern with rank at or below $ \lfloor d_R/2 \rfloor $, where $ d_R $ denotes the standard rank metric code distance established by Gabidulin. Furthermore, we show these codes achieve a symmetric packing distance of at least $ \lfloor 2d_R/3 \rfloor $.

### 2. Decoding Algorithm Development
Building upon the first finding presents an efficient decoding algorithm capable of correcting all symmetric error patterns with rank up to $ \lfloor d_R/2 \rfloor + 1 $. In addition to this algorithmic approach, we explore the dual code properties related to covering distance by formulating several associated Al-Terry forms.

### Conclusion
Finally, leveraging these structural dual properties allows us to derive additional algorithms that correct a broad class of error patterns defined by rank $ d' $, where $ d' $ satisfies the inequality $ \lfloor d_R/2 \rfloor + 1 \leq d' \leq d_R $.

Building upon \cite{Fitzpatrick:2016fug}, we derive integral representations for OPE blocks associated with spinning primaries possessing arbitrary spin and conformal dimension when OPE blocks are constructed from conformal families. Employing this representation in OPE channel decomposition of CFT four-point correlation functions, we determine the measure governing OPE blocks within spinning conformal towers. We simulate two dark matter scenarios employing both $N$-body and semi-analytical methods to test whether dark matter can acquire measurable velocities from primordial scalar gravitational potential interactions. Healthcare providers are increasingly recognizing the Social Determinants of Health (SDoH)—the extrinsic, community-level influences shaping individual well-being—as a priority for addressing health disparities and lowering costs, yet there remains no consensus on the specific SDoH factors most critical in clinical contexts. Given the scarcity of structured electronic health record (EHR) data regarding SDoH, this study utilizes unstructured, implicit data mined from social media to generate EHR-compatible SDoH insights. By leveraging text mining techniques applied to patient-typed entries in Twitter messages and physician-authored clinical notes, the research demonstrates that while both contain similar implicit information, their overlap is not random; specific implicit SDoH content appears frequently in both datasets but with distinct content frequencies and distribution patterns requiring further analysis.

This study investigates a two-link swimmer, also known as the Purcell swimmer, which functions as a basic model for biological entities like protozoa and operates by undergoing periodic shape changes. By applying Newton's second law to establish the motion equations within a two-dimensional viscous fluid—governed by a low Reynolds number environment—we analyze how traditional self-propulsion compares to alternative strategies like drift-based movement. Our simulation results demonstrate that, in terms of displacement after a single actuation cycle, a drift-based approach can surpass conventional propulsion by up to tenfold. Furthermore, we identify a specific singular curve within the parameter space associated with singular non-motile states; traversing a trajectory near this curve enables supermotility. Analysis of the underlying mechanisms attributes this enhanced motion to a resonant interaction between the swimmer's shape transformations and its translational and rotational velocities.

Urban physical contacts and social networking have been linked to surges in a nation's economic output, innovation, and overall prosperity. Nevertheless, the direct impact of cities' spatial "meeting-geography" on foreign direct investment (FDI) and broader business creation requires further study. Drawing on a comprehensive dataset of nearly three decades of U.S. FDI figures, our research reveals that the spatial distribution of such investment is sensitive to localized FDI "frictions," reflecting contact intensity and transportation expenses. Additionally, our findings indicate that the geographic distribution of FDI mirrors a "home bias," favoring locations around investment origins. The creation of FDI-friendly digital meeting platforms could help alleviate these spatial barriers and boost investment volumes.

We post-processed pre-brotating disk three-dimensional (3D) hydrodynamics simulations of high-mass young stellar objects (MYOs) to analyze an unexplained anomalous event: a ~200-day accretion burst displaying a distinct, sharp decline. This mechanism generates the burst and determines its specific profile. Consequently, features in such bursts serve as a means to probe and understand disk structures and dynamics that control accretion processes in high-mass stars.
