This research investigates the two-dimensional water wave problem characterized by an irrotational, incompressible fluid subject to constant shear. Naviging dynamic and unstructured outdoor environments remains a significant challenge for autonomous platforms. This study introduces a novel decoding order designed to mitigate security challenges among nonorthogonal multiple access users with unsecured access. Initially, we analytically determine the total count of possible decoding sequences. Addressing outliers in dimensionality reduction, this paper proposes a semantic alignment method grounded in $\ell_1$-norm principal component analysis (L1-PCA), which enhances robustness compared to conventional approaches yet currently lacks an effective optimization strategy for high-dimensional tasks. Annotated data regarding individual instances are fundamental to most supervised learning methodologies. Nevertheless, re-annotating data after modifying evaluation metrics or baseline models is typically resource-intensive. This paper introduces "BERT-Label," a method that leveraged BERT to convert evaluation data into evaluation standards, thereby facilitating rapid parameter training. By utilizing pre-trained language representations, BERT-Label enables the efficient acquisition of annotated labels for dialog evaluation without necessitating extensive manual labor, thus supporting agile development cycles. Empirical results demonstrate that BERT-Label generates labels superior to those provided by a single human annotator and rivals the accuracy of teams of annotators. Furthermore, this approach allows for rapid model evaluation and training; researchers can assess the performance of eight specific baselines across three datasets within a single afternoon and obtain an evaluated model for each within two hours.

At ICALP 2006, Kopczyński hypothesized that the class of prefix-independent half-positional winning conditions remains closed under the formation of finite unions. On finite arenas, we disprove this conjecture. To achieve this, we propose a novel category of prefix-independent bi-positional winning conditions known as energy conditions, utilizing the framework of totally ordered groups. As a subclass of Magnetic Cataclysmic Variables (CVs), asynchronously rotating polars remain poorly understood compared to the well-studied polars. This paper analyzes fresh, high-exposure, long-exposure, and time-resolved data for PSR JI630 - 3754 (uniquely renamed as ANXUSIAMETI C V-1), an asynchronously polar source. The observations include both new and existing scintillation and optical light curve data. ANXUSIAMETI C V-1 exhibits a wide range of spin period and spin period derivative values, which are anomalous for typical polars. Its spin period derivative is particularly high, exceeding those found even in X-ray emitters by several orders of magnitude. This study also analyzes the source's optical emission geometry using light curve data, revealing that the X-ray emision region is closely aligned with, though slightly offset from, the main emision pole. The paper further evaluates the feasibility of PSR X as an X-ray source using emision model calculations, finding that while emision from a point source is plausible, a dipole alignment configuration better fits the observed data. This research concludes that more research and observation are required to fully understand the nature and behavior of these mysterious sources. ANXUSIAMETI C V-1's unique characteristics challenge existing theories, suggesting that it represents a distinct class of objects rather than just an outlier among standard polars.

This study investigates the electronic and magnetic properties of TiO$_2$ doped with non-magnetic impurities, utilizing first-principles calculations. We specifically examine substitutional doping where carbon and nitrogen replace titanium, as well as interstitial carbon and nitrogen configurations. Our results indicate that isolated C and N atoms in substitutional sites induce local magnetic moments of 2 $\mu_B$ each, generating electronic states within the band gap that stabilize small polaron formations. In contrast, interstitial carbon and nitrogen generate magnetic interactions distinct from the substitutional case. Furthermore, a mixed C/N substitution results in a spin-polarized surface resembling reduced metallic TiO$_2$, while this specific configuration proves unstable due to strong driving forces for atomic migration toward substitutional positions. We also evaluated the influence of pre-existing oxygen vacancies on these systems.

X-ray observations of the hot gas in the intra-cluster medium reveal extensive data on galaxy cluster dynamics, particularly regarding the violent mergers that shape their diverse structural properties. While thermal gravitational instability and tidal forces are well-understood drivers of gas evolution, the mechanisms and significance of non-thermal pressure support remain less clearly defined. This study evaluates both observational data and numerical simulations to determine the sources, relative importance, and temporal evolution of non-thermal pressure in both typical and disturbed cluster environments. Using a maximum entropy method applied to profile data from XMM-Newton and Suzaku, alongside comparison with similar analyses from simulations, the research derives gas profiles perpendicular to cluster cores. The work finds that the outer regions of most clusters exhibit clear signatures of non-thermal support, closely aligning with the turbulent velocity predictions from simulations based on primary shocks generated during mergers. Furthermore, a distinct excess pressure perpendicular to the rotation axis is identified in the outskirts of merging clusters—a phenomenon also replicated in simulations. This excess is most strongly associated with shock-turbulence dynamics rather than just general activity. These findings offer crucial constraints on the physical modeling required for accurate reconstruction of merger histories and suggest that this anomalous pressure effect serves as a valuable indicator of recent cluster merging.

Magnetic fields observed in A-type stars, white dwarfs, and neutron stars are renowned for their long-term persistence, yet the internal physical processes enabling these states remain an area of ongoing research. Formal proofs have demonstrated that neither strictly toroidal nor entirely poloidal fields remain stable indefinitely. Conversely, numerical experiments have validated the stability of configurations that are roughly axisymmetric, composed of intertwined toroidal and poloidal elements within a stably stratified twisted torus structure. Although earlier work suggested general upper and lower bounds for the relative intensity of these fields, our goal is to refine these limits by heavily utilizing modern high-resolution finite element methods (FEM). Employing a variational approach for the magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) energy equation, we executed a straightforward label-search procedure to test specific geometries. Our refined calculations indicate that for the particular class of fields examined, the most rigorous constraint shifts to a lower bound of $\mathcal{O}(1.15)$, whereas the permissible upper limit potentially extends as high as $\mathcal{order}(100)$, contingent upon the specific model parameters.

The implementation of flow equations within the FRG enables research progress by circumventing the direct solution of the full theory, instead integrating only the effective average action along a trajectory defined by a single parameter, the renormalization scale. Within systems exhibiting symmetry breaking, the fixed-point structure of these equations determines critical exponents. Recent efforts have focused on enhancing computational efficiency through linearization schemes, which decouple quantum fluctuations in the Polchinski equation to achieve exact results. In this investigation, we demonstrate that such methods can also be successfully adapted to the Wetterich equation. Furthermore, we show that employing a rank-1 projection for the wave function operator square yields simpler, exact solutions.

The study utilizes 8-10 micron data derived from the new IRIS 200" mosaic to determine the total masses of protostellar cores and starless cores within the infrared dark clouds (IDCs) known to lie in the Galactic disk surrounding the Sun. By cross-referencing this data with 1.1 mm continuum observations from the Submillimeter Array (SMA), we cross-identified 47 cores with masses ranging between 1.6 and 43.3 solar masses ($M_\odot$). A primary distinction found is that protostellar cores possess significantly higher masses than starless cores, a discrepancy we suggest may be attributed to lower star formation efficiency or initial mass function variations in IDCs compared to typical clouds. Additionally, these cores are spatially linked to H i absorption features detected by ILAS II, suggesting most are embedded within them. Finally, the paper presents evidence that cores identified via mid-infrared emission at this millimeter wavelength are likely not obscured at longer submillimeter bands.

G\"odel modal logics extend intuitionistic modal logic through the addition of the prelinearity axiom, and this article concentrates on their algebraic and relational semantics, employing the essential tools of pointwise operations within a Heyting space. Significant attention is given to characterizing axiomatic extensions of basic G\"odel modal logic via equivalences defined by 4-valued pointwise K\"odel algebras built over the complex numbers $\mathbb{C}_4$, and these derived logics are fully presented. Furthermore, relational characterizations are provided for various levels of the Spa\'n extension series attached to the core modal logic.

LiDAR point clouds capture detailed, high-resolution 3D representations of the world and are utilized across a range of applications, including urban and environmental monitoring scene understanding, autonomous vehicle perception, robotics, and disaster recovery. However, acquiring LiDAR data remains expensive and time-consuming. Consequently, this study introduces synthetic, high-frequency (HF) LiDAR-based simulated environments to enhance the ability of machine learning models. These vast simulated environments consist of physically consistent point clouds and intrinsically include corresponding depth maps, instance segmentation labels, and 3D model annotations. Furthermore, this research presents the "HF-LiDAR-3D-Set," a multi-annotation benchmark specifically designed to evaluate performance in scene understanding, object detection, and reconstruction using highly frequent sampled laser data. Additionally, this paper offers a new framework for efficient point cloud reconstruction and a training strategy for point-to-point (PtP) translation that leverages intrinsic semantic labels to improve the alignment of point-to-point transformations based on point-to-image (PtI) visual-inertial (PtI) constraints from depth-based projections. Experimental results confirm that this approach significantly enhances the performance of downstream applications such as semantic segmentation and 3D reconstruction when compared to frequently used heterogeneous point cloud benchmarks like SemanticKITTI and Waymo Open Scene.

The source of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), defined as particles with energies exceeding $10^{20}$ eV, has long been a major unsolved problem in astrophysics. The alpha-alpha hadronic cascade neutrino model offers a framework to address this by accounting for the full energy history of cosmic rays, from their primordial origins in cosmological epochs up to their final annihilation in the present day. By relying on well-established, straightforward general-relativistic cosmological principles, this model naturally generates energy spectra peaking around $10^{22}$ eV that align closely with the "anomaly" of highest-energy neutrinos recently detected by the Tunka-133 observatory. Furthermore, the predicted peak energy for most species matches the observed ankle feature in the primary UHECR spectrum at approximately $4\times 10^{18}$ eV; notably, these anomalies are resolved by the model's conclusion that such cannot constitute the peak component itself. Ultimately, this approach functions as a generic, generic mechanism likely operative in nature, potentially resolving these anomalies through the specific properties of the Tully-Levis alpha-Levi Tunka-Levis system, while also predicting secondary highest-energy cosmic rays as evidence for the existence of highest-energy neutrinos in Tunka-Levis.

The rheology of complex liquids is highly sensitive to interfacial roughness conditions. By correlating stress assessments with visual observations of various moving rough interfaces within dry liquid foams, this study reveals three distinct mechanical regimes: slipplase, stick-slip motion, and anchored soap films. The measured stresses in the slipplase and anchored regimes align with established models, while a new lever rule theory is proposed to characterize stresses in the stick-slip scenario. Ultimately, the prevalence of either stick-slip or anchorage behaviors is dictated by roughness factor—defined as the proportion of surface asperity relative to Plateau border curvature radius.

In ISIC challenge 2019 tasks 1 and 2, we ranked 3rd and 4th utilizing this project to provide diagnoses for skin lesions based on medical images and auxiliary metadata, despite nine classes where one does not appear in the actual data. Our solution employs an ensemble strategy combining five models, processing image and text inputs separately before merging results to diagnose lesion types. Text features were derived using a single sentence encoder, whereas image features were generated by one such convolutional network; fused embeddings were classified by a fully connected layer, with our custom components proving superior to three advanced multi-modal approaches we also tested, validating the efficacy of well-tuned individual components over complex architectures.

This study investigates the stationary fingers arising in a rotating Hele-Shaw cell, focusing on an elastic membrane separating two fluids with distinct densities under constant angular velocity. By deriving an explicit polar representation of the membrane's shape and employing potential flow theory, we established the governing equations for this hydrodynamic problem. Our analysis examines how finger emergence is influenced by the membrane's elastic properties, the density contrast, centrifugal forces, and hydrodynamic interactions. Results indicate that increasing membrane elasticity, increasing the density difference, or increasing hydrodynamic effects all tend to stabilize the interface; conversely, these factors can delay the onset of finger formation by significantly increasing wavenumber and amplitude of initial irregularities. Numerical solutions for the membrane's steady configurations were obtained via iteration, with initial estimates generated through the application of regular boundary conditions.

This paper extends nonequilibrium thermodynamics to systems that cannot reach a steady state of mechanical equilibrium by integrating recent findings on work and heat definitions. A key contribution is the identification of a universal mechanism for **free expansion**, applicable across diverse fields—from isolated gases to open quantum systems—where **microwork** briefly shifts to a negative sign immediately following the onset of expansion, reversibly transitioning to negative osmotic work and driving the phenomenon. We further explore the consequences of these results for understanding irreversible processes and the application of fluctuation theorems in systems that never stabilize.

### Key Points and Explanations

- **Extension of Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics**: Existing frameworks are updated to incorporate modern insights regarding work and heat in out-of-equilibrium scenarios.
- **Free Expansion Mechanism**: Through mathematical derivation, a general explanation for free expansion has been provided, showing that it results from the transient transition of **microwork** to negative values.
- **Reversible Transition to Negative Osmotic Work**: The temporarily negative microwork converts into negative osmotic work, which is essential for the observed behavior in various systems, including quantum open systems.
- **Understanding Irreversibility and Fluctuation Theorems**: These mechanisms offer new perspectives on broader nonequilibrium phenomena, facilitating a deeper comprehension of irreversible processes and the underlying fluctuation theorems when systems do not achieve mechanical or thermal equilibrium.

Curiosity serves as the fundamental drive for learning, holding significant potential for nurturing student creativity and a passion for education within classrooms. Research methodology involved semi-structured interviews conducted with 15 undergraduate participants. We introduce a new stationary Gaussian process prior defined on undirected graphs with no self-loops, built using the graph Laplacian and its localizability. This model extends stationary Gaussian processes from the Euclidean space to graphs and comes with a closed-form hypergraph PDF. We derive efficient computational techniques for inference and simulation under these new processes without sacrificing scalability. Theory shows that this formulation captures both transitivity and decay characteristics seen in graph-valenced degree sequences. Numerical experiments demonstrate its superiority over current methods for generating random networks with a realistic distribution of degree values.

Monitoring the city road infrastructure plays a vital role in enhancing the efficiency of transportation networks and addressing urban challenges. Nevertheless, existing practices relying on human observers and anecdotal reports face significant constraints regarding coverage, trustworthiness, and reliability. To overcome these deficits, this research leverages mobile phones and Deep Learning methodologies to establish an automatic system for detecting road obstacles and incidents. The proposed approach detects various obstacles—encompassing construction zones, accidents, and maintenance issues—as well as predicts immediate traffic states with notable accuracy. This paper investigates the implications of $J/\psi$ decays into undetectable states, focusing on light sterile neutrinos and dark matter (DM) with masses below the GeV scale. We employ low-energy Effective Field Theories (EFTs) to model general neutrino interactions alongside Dirac fermion DM interacting with charm quarks. For radiative decays of the type $J/\psi \to \nu_i \nu_j X$, where $X$ is any hadron, we derive broad branching ratio formulas valid for all cases except those yielding single light sterile neutrinos, which are constrained by lepton flavor violation limits. Additional limits on dark matter properties arise not only from $\gamma$-factory searches but also from deviations in muon-to-electron relic density and single-event DM direct detection experiments, particularly in the sub-MeV mass range. Furthermore, these radiative decays present a promising signature for Beyond Standard Model (BSM) physics at the High-Luminosity $e^+e^-$ collider (CEPC), offering enhanced sensitivity to light sterile neutrinos and light dark matter compared to other current constraints.

Second derivation-based general linear methods (SGLMs) have been extensively studied because general linear methods are versatile for addressing ordinary differential equation initial value problems. In this paper, we specifically examine the order barriers attainable by second-squared-sigmoidal (SG2) class methods. By applying decimation techniques to a particular fully implicit SG2 method and employing a partial linearization strategy to derive an explicit update step, we demonstrate that fully explicit SG2 methods exist which achieve second-order accuracy. Furthermore, by fully linearizing an existing implicit SG2 method to obtain a one-stage implicit function, our results indicate that the maximum stage-order matching can be realized up to the second order for implicit functions. These approaches represent novel contributions, as previous research had established these order barriers solely within the context of the basic implicit stage of the method. In the context of optimization and numerical simulation, where computational cost is often better controlled through the use of implicit techniques, the development of these novel implicit update schemes offers a promising advantage over standard options. Additionally, these examples provide a beneficial counterpoint to the frequent limitation of general linear methods when employed as a framework for constructing full implicit algorithms.

This study establishes Multivariate Functional Singular Spectrum Analysis (MFSSA), the functional extension capable of operating alongside singular spectral analysis (SSA). To begin, we define the requisite framework for multivariate functional time series. Following this by adapting pre-ssA techniques for multivariate functional data, we introduce the MFSSA procedure itself, allowing for the reconstruction of smooth, continuous curves rather than simple data points. This approach relies on Functional Kernel Principal Component Analysis (FK-PCA); assuming single observations of functional objects, FK-PCA facilitates dimension reduction while preserving continuity. We provide the asymptotic distribution necessary for significance testing within the MFSSA context. Using simulated simulations, we demonstrate the capability of MFSSA to detect cyclic components and smooth structures, and finally, we apply the methodology to a case study examining the morphological variations observed in brain images across different cognitive states.

Deep-learning-driven Automatic Essay Scoring (AES) tools have become increasingly popular in recent years, attracting significant research attention due to their apparent efficacy and operational feasibility. However, despite the proliferation of these scoring algorithms, there is currently no widely accepted benchmark for evaluating them. The situation mirrors the historical lack of standards in AES evaluation prior to the integration of deep learning. The primary obstacle hindering the development of an benchmark for modern deep-learning based AES systems is the difficulty in gathering sufficient large-scale, annotated essay data necessary for training purposes. To bridge this gap, the Authored Essays Evaluation Benchmark (AEVB) framework is proposed. Central to AEVB are two core strategies: first, leveraging existing authentic but unannotated essays rather than relying on synthetic data generation; and second, employing a differential evaluation approach that facilitates performance assessment using limited annotated data. Together with these principles, the AEVB framework successfully delivers a robust standard for evaluating automatic scoring algorithms designed for large datasets and leveraging deep learning technologies.

In reinforcement learning, exogenous state variables can introduce unpredictable variance into rewards, thereby decelerating the learning process. Smart contracts serve as fundamental building blocks of blockchain ecosystems, yet deriving them from formal specifications via automated methods remains a significant hurdle. These contracts govern critical operations, such as monetary transfers and voting processes, where ensuring correctness is essential, and while formal methods facilitate this, the final implementation must ultimately be validated through property verification. Unfortunately, defects in these contracts can have severe repercussions; for instance, the Bitfinere cryptocurrency exchange lost approximately $74 million due to a flawed smart contract designed for auditing and tracking asset origins using Provenance. To bring Provenance to life, engineers deployed a smart contract for authorization and established a quorum mechanism based on a byzantine fault-tolerant (BFT) consensus algorithm. However, prior to deployment, this contract required thorough verification. Addressing this gap, our paper presents an informal examination and formal encoding in the Coq proof assistant of the specific Libra/Choco implementation used for Provenance's smart contract and its BFT quorum system. Furthermore, we demonstrate the verification of key invariants related to authorisation and BFT consensus properties following this encoding process.

Ultrasound elastography represents a promising noninvasive method for visualizing tissue mechanics by analyzing deformation and wave propagation following the application of external mechanical forces. However, these techniques are constrained by the low spatial resolution inherent to the required physical motion, often limiting their clinical efficacy. Although High-Resolution Magnetic Resonance Elastography achieves superior results through high frequencies and large strain ranges achieved via vibration, ultrasound elastography seeks to match this performance through Virtual Source Synthetic Shearing Aperture (VSSA). This technique employs a Hadamard matrix sequence to encode displacement patterns across tissue samples using a contact transducer, allowing for the isolation of individual wave sources and subsequent back-propagation to reconstruct elastograms with enhanced spatial accuracy. While effective in theory, the practical utility of VSSA is currently hindered by the necessity for a rigidly fixed tissue sample, demanding additional hardware to stabilize biological tissues. To address this limitation, we adapted the VSSA framework for live animal models by replacing the tissue-equivalent phantom in a rabbit model, yielding clear visual representation of shear waves originating from the VSSA processing. Comparative analysis shows that standard SA elastograms generated from the same data exhibit significant image artifacts, whereas the VSSA results provide distinct, accurate wave imaging. Future investigations will refine the decoding algorithms used in VSSA reconstruction and extend the methodology to in vivo human subjects.

Sequential sampling is employed when a population is unknown beforehand, and information is gathered in successive single or group observations. Calibrating an eye-in-hand camera is both a fundamental and extensively studied topic in robotics. Numerous techniques for estimating camera poses have been developed, leveraging either point clouds or range images. Since each individual method carries inherent weaknesses, a robust solution requires integrating multiple approaches. Although research fusing several point cloud-based algorithms exists, fusion of point cloud and image sensor methods remains underdeveloped. This study introduces a modular, systematic framework designed to combine multiple pose estimation algorithms to produce an optimal output. We implement this concept by merging three distinct point cloud techniques along with two image sensor approaches into a unified point cloud-Image (PCI) framework. Specifically, we adapt the Normal Distributions Transform (NDT) estimator by weighting its objective function using data derived from epipolar geometry, Semi-Direct Sparse, and Correspondence-by-Features (CBF) algorithms. Evaluation across diverse datasets demonstrates that this combined framework consistently achieves higher precision compared to any single constituent algorithm.

Inverse problems involve reconstructing an image from noisy, degraded, or incomplete observations. While maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation is frequently used for these tasks, it often fails to capture uncertainty regarding the reconstructed images. In this work, we propose a novel approach that generates diverse samples from the posterior distribution by leveraging the relationship between the MAP solution and generative models. Specifically, our findings indicate that if a generative model can be formulated as the sum of a generative operator and a constrained operator—similar to the structure used in augmented Lagrangian methods or sparse hierarchical Gaussian models (SHGMs), which can solve various inverse problems—it is possible to approximate these posterior samples. Crucially, this approximation can achieve a similar solution quality to the original generative model but requires significantly fewer iterations. We demonstrate that this framework applies to a broad range of problems, including denoising, deblurring, and compressed sensing.

Most scattering screens found within the interstellar medium have unknown properties due to the complex, non-linear relationship between observational radio scintillation effects and the underlying electron density inhomogeneities. However, for screens exhibiting linear regimes, standard fitting methods can determine both the total screen thickness (along the line of sight), denoted as $L$, and the transverse irregularity scale, denoted as $r_{\rm T}$. We have developed a novel statistical inference approach that utilizes Monte Carlo techniques to estimate screens operating in the regime where they are not linear, specifically by analyzing diffracted scintillation observations. Through mock datasets and real-case applications involving screens at specific distances ($L$) and transverse scales ($r_{\rm T}$), we demonstrate the methodology's capability to identify screens in their non-linear regimes, effectively distinguishing them from those in the linear regime, and accurately deriving the values for $L$ and $r_{\rm T}$. Conversely, for screens where the absolute scale is uncertain (unnormalized), this method can reliably identify the correct non-linear regime, provided the screen resides beyond the Galactic plane and the observation frequency is sufficiently high to ensure the screen is sufficiently thin. Consequently, this approach facilitates the investigation of screens currently accessible only through radio scintillation analysis.

This work is driven by the objective to identify the spatial origins of any sound within video content. Existing approaches typically rely on audio-visual cross-modal attention, using mined audio spectra to guide visual inspection; however, these methods overlook direct supervision from sound cues during the mining phase and struggle to adapt the visual network for localization beyond general focusing. To address what we term as limited visual supervision signals, we propose exploring visual supervision that leverages the inherent visual difficulty of examples themselves specifically for localization tasks. To actualize hardened sample mining that aligns audio with visual features for more effective localization, we introduce "audio-guided visual hard sample mining." This involves three key strategies: first, computing visual difficulty based on the clarity of the visible sound source; second, calculating example difficulty according to the mismatch between predicted localization outputs and input audio spectra (which we call "spectrum loss"); and third, jointly optimizing the visual encoder and an output head that maps visual contexts to localization results using targeted visual supervision from visual features, distinct from the audio supervision. Experiments on the public "Echolocation" dataset demonstrate a 0.4 improvement in average hourly location error (AHL) compared to the baseline, rising to 0.44 when limited to videos where hearing is possible in the source. This indicates our approach successfully learns visual representations better suited for audio-visual localization, effectively utilizing supervisory information from both the audio queries and visual difficulties.

Speech Translation involves converting spoken audio in one language into written text in another. Traditional neural approaches typically depend on large amounts of labeled training data, including speech-to-text pairs and bilingual speech-text combinations. The primary challenge in speech translation lies in its difficulty, generated by the diverse modality changes from speech to text across different languages; currently, no efficient approach exists to bridge this gap without substantial datasets. These limitations highlight the need for data-efficient techniques capable of handling modal variances with fewer samples. We introduce a novel framework utilizing few-shot learning and adapter tuning to enable zero-shot translation through few-shot training, eliminating the requirement for target-language speech-to-text data. Furthermore, we introduce Continuous Projection Adapters (CPA), which replace standard transformer feed-forward networks and substantially lessen the need for parameter fine-tuning. Extensive evaluations across the Compass and MuSe datasets demonstrate the model's capacity for zero-shot translation using only a handful of training samples.
